chapter.title: Pressure, Winds, Storms, and Cyclones
chapter.summary: This chapter explores how pressure is created by force acting on an area and how it affects everything from your school bag straps to massive weather systems. You will learn how differences in air pressure create winds and how rising warm air leads to powerful storms and cyclones. By understanding these concepts, we can explain everyday things like why we use sharp knives and how to stay safe during a lightning strike or a cyclone.
key_points: Pressure is defined as the force acting per unit area (Pressure = Force / Area).
The SI unit of pressure is the Pascal (Pa), which is equal to 1 Newton per square metre (N/m²).
Broad straps or handles reduce pressure by spreading force over a larger area.
Liquid pressure increases as the height of the liquid column increases.
Liquids and gases exert pressure in all directions, including on the walls of their containers.
The envelope of air around Earth exerts atmospheric pressure on everything.
Air always moves from a region of high pressure to a region of low pressure, creating wind.
High-speed winds are accompanied by a reduction in air pressure.
Thunderstorms form when warm, moist air rises and creates static electric charges in clouds.
Lightning is a sudden flow of electric charges between clouds or between a cloud and the ground.
Cyclones are massive spinning storms that form over warm ocean waters due to low pressure.
The calm center of a cyclone is called the 'eye,' while the surrounding area has high-speed winds.

You must have observed fallen leaves on the ground swirling in the air or being swept away, and trees swaying or even bending when a strong wind blows. Have you ever wondered why fallen leaves rise in the air or trees sway or bend? Does the wind exert force on fallen leaves to make them rise or on trees to bend? Recall other similar effects of the force exerted by wind like slamming of doors or rattling of windows, or fluttering of clothes? How does the force exerted by wind make this happen? The force exerted by wind creates wind pressure which causes these effects. In this chapter, we will explore the relationship between force and pressure, and understand how they shape powerful natural events like thunderstorms and cyclones.
6.1 Pressure

Megha and her brother Pawan are going on a picnic. They walk to the picnic spot, carrying identical items in their bags (Fig. 6.1). On the way , Pawan keeps adjusting his bag, and looks uncomfortable. Megha asks, “Is there a problem with your bag?” Pawan responds, “Yes, it is hurting my shoulders.” Megha says, “Both our bags are equally heavy. Why does your bag hurt, and mine doesn’t?” Pawan reflects for a minute and says, “Perhaps, it is because of the difference in the straps of our bags. My bag has narrow straps while your bag has broad straps.” Can the shape or size of the straps really make a difference? Let us try to find out. When we carry a bag, we feel its weight because of the force of gravity acting on our shoulders. The weight of the bag with narrow straps acts on a smaller area of our shoulders, whereas the weight of the bag with broad straps is spread out over a larger area of our shoulders. It is due to this reason that we feel more comfortable carrying a bag with broader straps than one with narrow straps, although both bags have the same weight. Since the area over which the force acts is involved, we define a quantity called pressure, which is the force per unit area. So,   Pressure = ForceArea At this stage, we will consider only those forces which act perpendicular to the surface on which the pressure is to be computed.
Fig. 6.1: Megha and Pawan
carrying their bags

Broad straps reduce the pressure exerted by the bag on our shoulders as compared to narrow straps. Therefore, we feel more comfortable carrying a bag with broad straps. Can you now understand why it feels easier to lift a water-filled bucket with a broad handle than with a narrow handle (Fig. 6.2)? Similarly, we have seen that when people carry loads like pots or vegetable baskets on their heads, they often place a round piece of cloth under the loads (Fig. 6.3). In both cases, the objective is to reduce pressure by increasing the area over which the weight acts. Pressure is defined as the force per unit area. The SI unit of force is newton and that of area is metre 2. Therefore, the SI unit of pressure is newton/metre2 (N/m2). This unit is also called a pascal, denoted by Pa. What can you conclude from your observations in Table 6.1? We conclude that when the area over which a force applied is smaller, the resulting pressure is higher, making it easier to do certain tasks. This is why it is easier to drive a nail using its pointed end, and it is easier to cut an apple with the sharp edge of a knife. You must have seen overhead water tanks (Fig. 6.4) in your locality, or on the rooftops of houses used for water supply . Why are these tanks always placed at a height? Do liquids also exert pressure? Let us find out by conducting the following activity.
Activity 6.1: Let us try and find out
z Take two transparent glass or plastic pipes of the same
length (about 25 cm), but of different diameters, as shown in Fig. 6.5.

same extent? What can you infer from this activity? You must have observed that the two balloons bulge to the same extent. Why is it so? Notice that because of the different diameters, the weight of water in the two pipes is different. However, the bulge in both the balloons is the same. This means that the weight of water in the pipes could not be responsible for the extent of the bulge of the balloons. Could it be that the water column is exerting pressure? Yes, it is the pressure exerted by the water column which is responsible for the bulge. That is why equal water column heights produce equal bulges in the balloons, despite their different diameters.

Pour some more water in any one of the pipes used in Fig. 6.5. Observe the bulge of the balloon. Repeat this process a few times, adding more water each time and noting the extent of bulge as shown in Fig. 6.6. Do you see any relation between the amount of bulge of the rubber balloon and the height of the water column in the pipe? You must have observed that the bulge of the balloon increases as the height of the water column increases. Thus, as the height of the water column in the pipe increases, the pressure at the bottom of the pipe also increases, which causes the balloon to bulge more. So, we can say that the pressure exerted by a liquid in a vessel depends on the height of its column. This is the reason why overhead tanks are placed at a height so that the pressure in the taps is increased, resulting in a good stream of water from the taps. Therefore, we can conclude that liquids exert pressure not only at the bottom of the container, but also on its sides. In fact liquids exert pressure in all directions. Do you know that the base of a dam is much broader than the top? This is because a broad base  not only supports the structure of the dam, but also withstands the horizontal

water pressure near the bottom (Fig. 6.8). The water stored in the dam, exerts pressure horizontally on the side walls of the dam and vertically on the floor due to the height of the water level. The pressure which acts horizontally, is very large near its bottom. Thus, to withstand the pressure, the base of the dam is made broader.

6.2 Pressure Exerted by Air

You already know that air is all around us. The envelope of air surrounding the Earth is called atmosphere. The atmospheric air contains nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide, and other gases in small quantities. The atmosphere extends up to many kilometres above the surface of the Earth. Let us find out if the atmosphere exerts pressure by performing the following activity.
Activity 6.3: Let us explore

You would have observed that more effort is needed to lift the paper plate when it is covered with the unfolded chart paper, than with the folded chart paper. When we cover the paper plate with unfolded chart paper, the area of the covering sheet increases. The effort needed to lift the paper plate increases. Notice that the weight of the covering sheet has not changed. What can you infer from this? We can infer from these observations that air exerts force on the covering sheet, which makes it difficult to lift the paper plate. Moreover, this force increases with

As force per unit area is pressure, we can conclude that air exerts pressure on the paper sheet. In fact, air exerts pressure on all objects. The pressure exerted by air around us is known as the atmospheric pressure. You must have experienced that when you blow air into a balloon, it gets inflated. Why? This is because the air being filled inside the balloon exerts pressure on the walls of the balloon (Fig 6.10). Can we say that air exerts pressure in all directions? Yes, that is why the balloon expands in all directions. What happens when an inflated balloon is kept without closing its mouth? The air escapes from the balloon. Why does the air escape from the balloon?
Have you ever wondered how large the atmospheric pressure is? Let us get an idea about its magnitude by performing the following activity.
Activity 6.4: Let us perform
z Take a good-quality rubber sucker. Press it firmly against a
smooth flat surface (Fig. 6.11).
z Do you realise that it sticks to the surface?
z Now, try to pull it off. Do you find it difficult to pull it off?

When we press the sucker, most of the air between its cup and the surface on which it is placed is pushed out and the air pressure inside it is reduced. The sucker sticks to the surface because the pressure of air surrounding the sucker is higher than the pressure exerted by the air inside the sucker. To pull the sucker off the surface, the applied force should be strong enough to overcome the pressure difference between outside the sucker and inside the sucker. Do you know how large the atmospheric pressure is? The force exerted by the atmospheric air column over an area 15 cm × 15 cm is nearly equal to the force of gravity on an object of mass 225 kg (2250 N). The reason we are not crushed under this weight is that the pressure inside our bodies is also equal to the atmospheric pressure. This balances the pressure exerted from outside. The pressure inside our body is caused by the movement of fluids and gases in tissues and organs of the body.
6.3 Formation of Wind

You must have noticed that on some days, the wind blows strongly, whereas on other days, it is calm. Sometimes, wind becomes so strong that it causes damage to life and property. You must have seen that when an inflated balloon is kept without closing its mouth, the air from the balloon escapes. Recall that when there is a puncture in the bicycle tube, the air escapes and the tube collapses. In both of these cases, does air move from a high pressure region to a low pressure region? The SI unit of pressure is N/m2, also known as pascal (Pa). However, the practical unit of air pressure is millibar (mb), which is equal to 100 Pa. Air pressure is also expressed in hectopascal (hPa), which is equal to 100 Pa.

What can be the reason for the change in the sizes of the balloons? The air pressure in the inflated balloon is higher than that in the uninflated balloon. As a result, some air moves from the inflated balloon to the uninflated balloon, resulting in changes in the size of both the balloons. Do you notice that after some time both the balloons attain almost the same size and the flow of air stops? Why does the air flow stop? The flow of air continues till the air pressure in the inflated balloon is higher than the air pressure in the uninflated balloon. The air flow stops when the pressure in both balloons becomes equal. At this stage, both balloons are almost of the same size. Thus, we can conclude that air moves from a region of high air pressure to a region of low air pressure. You can relate this conclusion to the directions of the sea breeze and land breeze, which you studied in Curiosity, Grade 7. As land gets heated faster than water during the day, the air above the land How do winds form? Does the difference in air pressure have anything to do with the formation of winds?

becomes warmer and lighter. Hence, it rises, creating an area of low pressure. The air from the high pressure region of the sea blows to the low pressure region which develops on the land, resulting in a sea breeze. At night, the water is warmer than the land. Therefore, a low pressure area develops above the sea. As a result, wind blows from the land to the sea, giving rise to land breeze. Thus, the phenomenon of land breeze and sea breeze is mainly due to the pressure differences over the land and the sea. If we could measure the speed of the escaping air in Activity 6.5, we would find that the speed of the air is higher if the pressure difference is higher. I have read that high-speed winds can blow off roofs. I wonder how?
6.4  High-Speed Winds Result in Lowering
of Air Pr essure
Activity 6.6: Let us observe
z Take two balloons of the same size.
z Inflate both balloons and tie strings to them.
z Hang the two balloons from a stick, leaving a
gap of 6–10 cm (Fig. 6.13).
z Now, blow air into the narrow space between
the balloons.
z What happens to the balloons? Note down
your observations.
z Now blow harder and observe.

When you blow between the two balloons, you observe that they move towards each other. This happens because when you blow air between the balloons, a low pressure area is created between them. The higher air pressure surrounding the balloon pushes them towards each other. You must have observed that blowing harder increases the speed at which the balloons approach each other. What can you infer from this activity? We infer that high speed winds are accompanied by a reduced air pressure.
Fig. 6.13: Blowing between two balloons

When high-speed winds blow over houses, a low-pressure area is created over them, as high-speed winds are accompanied by a reduced pressure. Therefore, the air pressure above the roofs of the houses is lower than the pressure below them. If the pressure difference is large and the roofs are weak, they may be blown away, as shown in Fig. 6.14  a. That is why it is safer to keep doors and windows of the houses open during storms with high-speed winds. When the same wind moves over the roofs, and through the houses, the pressure difference between inside of the houses and over the roofs is reduced to a large extent. This helps prevent the roofs from being blown off as shown in Fig. 6.14 b. You must have experienced that when high-speed winds blow during storms, they are sometimes accompanied by thunder and lightning. Let us learn more about them.
6.5 Storms, Thunderstorms, and Lightning
Fig. 6.14: (b) Roof of a house intact
Fig. 6.14: (a) Roof of a house

blown away Have you heard the sound of thunder and seen lightning during the rainy season? Yes, the sound of thunder is so frightening! Usually there is heavy rainfall too. When land gets heated, the warm and moist air, being lighter, rises, thereby creating a low pressure area. Cooler air from the surrounding high-pressure areas flows to take its place. This air, in turn, gets heated and rises. This results in a continuous process of wind circulation. As the rising air expands, it cools and moisture in it condenses to form water droplets, creating clouds. The water droplets merge to form heavier drops, which come down as rain, hail, or snow. The strong winds accompanied by rain is called a storm. In hot, humid, and tropical regions like India, storms are more frequent. Under certain conditions, warm air rises to great heights that the low temperature there converts water droplets into ice particles. Strong winds blowing upwards and downwards (Fig. 6.15) facilitate rubbing between water droplets

up and down Warm air Cool air

during lightning and ice particles. You have learnt in the chapter ‘Exploring Forces’ that when two objects are rubbed against each other, they get charged. In this case, strong winds blowing upwards and downwards and rubbing against each other cause static electric charges to develop within the clouds. The positively charged lighter ice particles move upwards and occupy the upper part of the clouds. The negatively charged heavier water droplets occupy the lower part of the clouds. Thus, a charge separation within the cloud takes place. Also, when the negatively charged lower part of the cloud moves closer to the ground, it causes the ground and nearby objects, such as trees or buildings, to become positively charged (Fig. 6.16). Normally, air acts as an electrical insulator and does not let opposite charges meet. But when the build up of charges becomes very large, the insulating property of air breaks down. A sudden flow of charges takes place, producing a bright flash of light called lightning. Lightning can occur as opposite charges collide within a cloud, between clouds, or between clouds and the ground. Lightning rapidly heats up the air around it, causing the air to expand and produce a loud sound known as thunder. A storm accompanied by lightning and thunder is called a thunderstorm.
A step further

Isolated and localised thunderstorms can sometimes occur in various regions of India. These thunderstorms are known by various names such as Kalboishakhi in West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand and Bordoisila in Assam. They occur before the arrival of the monsoon, thereby helping kharif crops to grow. In Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, they are known as mango showers as they support the ripening of mangoes. Local thunderstorms in Karnataka help in the growth of coffee plants. Lightning can be dangerous! It can ignite fires, damage buildings, and cause severe burns or death in humans and animals. We must take necessary precautions and protect ourselves from lightning. During lightning, stay away from tall objects, find a low-lying open area and crouch down, and minimise contact with the ground. Do not lie down flat. Avoid using an umbrella with a metallic rod. If you are in water, get out of it. If you are inside a bus or a car, you are comparatively safer.

This end is kept higher than the highest point of the building (Fig. 6.18). The other end of the rod is buried deep in the ground. 6.6 Cyclone

Cyclones are large storms that form over warm ocean waters. As the ocean water gets heated, the warm and moist air above it rises. As the moist air rises, the water vapour condenses to form raindrops. We know that during evaporation, water takes up heat to change into vapour. When this water vapour condenses into raindrops, heat is released back into the atmosphere. This causes further warming of the ascending air leading it to rise even further, creating an even lower pressure. Air from the surrounding regions rushes in and it also starts rising. Earth’s rotation causes the moving air to spin (Fig. 6.19). This cycle is repeated, resulting in the creation of a very low-pressure area with high-speed winds revolving around it. This spinning system of clouds, winds, and rain is called a cyclone. In a cyclone, the region of lowest pressure is at the centre, known as the eye of the cyclone. At the eye of the cyclone, the wind is calm, but the surrounding region experiences strong winds and heavy rainfall. As a cyclone moves from the ocean towards the land, it generates higher wind speeds compared to the wind speeds produced by regular thunderstorms. Once the cyclone reaches land, the source of moist air is cut off and it gradually loses its strength.

Even as a cyclone loses its strength while travelling over land, it leaves behind a trail of destruction that can take months or even years to repair. Cyclones can be extremely destructive. For example, the Amphan cyclone in 2020 had peak wind speeds of 270 km/h. Strong winds during a cyclone  push ocean water towards the shore, creating a wall of water that can be as high as 3–12 metres. This surge of water can flood coastal areas and even areas far from the sea. The heavy rainfall which accompanies a cyclone may cause rivers to overflow and can also trigger landslides. Seawater that rushes inland can contaminate drinking water sources and damage farmland. The salt in seawater can make soil less fertile, affecting crops. Roads may get blocked due to fallen trees and debris, making it difficult for help to reach the affected areas. Power outages can last for days, disrupting emergency services and daily life. How can we protect ourselves during cyclones? It is important to stay updated on weather reports and periodic alerts, and warnings issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD). Thanks to the weather monitoring satellites, today we can track cyclones and predict their path, helping us reduce their impact on life and property. Several national and international organisations work together to monitor cyclone-related disasters. If you live in a cyclone-prone area, keep an emergency kit ready with essential items. During a cyclone, quickly move to a nearby designated cyclone shelter.
Let us wrap up!

Cool air rushes to occupy the low-pressure area. Warm air rises, creating a low-pressure area. Warm air rises, cools, and the water vapour condenses to form clouds. Bigger water drops in the clouds fall to the ground as rain, hail, or snow. Positive and negative charges are created in the clouds by strong winds blowing upwards and downwards. Under certain weather conditions, storms may develop into cyclones. When positive and negative charges meet, they cause lightning. Lightning may occur within a cloud, between clouds, or between a cloud and the ground.

quiz.explain: High-speed air creates a low-pressure area, which is why the balloons actually move toward each other.

quiz.q: Which direction does wind blow?
options: From Low Pressure to High Pressure
From High Pressure to Low Pressure
quiz.explain: Air naturally rushes to fill areas where the pressure is lower, creating wind.

quiz.q: What is the 'eye' of a cyclone?
options: The area with the heaviest rain
The area with the highest wind speed
The part that hits the land first
quiz.explain: The eye is a unique, surprisingly calm region at the very center of the spinning storm.

quiz.q: During a thunderstorm, which particles usually move to the upper part of the cloud?
quiz.explain: Lighter, positively charged ice particles are carried upward by strong winds.

quiz.q: Why is the base of a dam made broader than the top?
options: To withstand higher water pressure at the bottom
To allow cars to drive on it
To prevent fish from jumping over
quiz.explain: Water pressure is much stronger at the bottom of the dam because of the height of the water above it.

quiz.q: What is the practical unit of air pressure used in weather reports, equal to 100 Pa?
quiz.explain: Meteorologists use millibars (mb) or hectopascals (hPa) to measure atmospheric pressure.

quiz.q: What name is given to pre-monsoon thunderstorms in Kerala and Karnataka?
quiz.explain: They are called mango showers because they help in the ripening of the mango crop.

quiz.q: Why don't we get crushed by the huge weight of the atmosphere?
options: Our bones are made of steel
The pressure inside our bodies balances the outside pressure
quiz.explain: The fluids and gases inside our tissues exert an outward pressure that matches the atmospheric pressure.

quiz.q: What is the safest thing to do if you are caught outside during lightning?
options: Hold an umbrella with a metal rod
Crouch low in an open area
Lie down flat on the ground
quiz.explain: Crouching low minimizes your height and contact with the ground, making you a less likely target.

ask_qa.q: Why does a school bag with thin straps hurt more than one with wide straps?
ask_qa.a: Thin straps have a smaller area, which increases the pressure on your shoulders. Wide straps spread the same weight over a larger area, reducing the pressure and making it more comfortable.

ask_qa.q: How does blowing over a piece of paper make it rise?
ask_qa.a: Blowing creates high-speed air over the paper, which reduces the air pressure on top. The higher pressure underneath the paper then pushes it upward.

ask_qa.q: Why do porters wear a round piece of cloth on their heads when carrying heavy loads?
ask_qa.a: The cloth increases the area of contact between the load and their head. By increasing the area, the pressure on their head is reduced, making the load easier to carry.

ask_qa.q: What causes the 'spark' and 'bang' of lightning and thunder?
ask_qa.a: Lightning is a massive flow of electricity that heats the air instantly. This heat causes the air to expand explosively, creating the loud sound wave we call thunder.

ask_qa.q: Why do cyclones lose strength once they reach land?
ask_qa.a: Cyclones get their energy from warm, moist air over the ocean. Once they move over land, they are cut off from this moisture source and gradually die out.

ask_qa.q: Why should we keep windows open during a very high-speed wind storm?
ask_qa.a: High-speed winds outside create low pressure over the roof. Keeping windows open helps equalize the pressure between the inside and outside, preventing the roof from being blown off.

ask_qa.q: How does a rubber sucker stick to a wall?
ask_qa.a: When pressed, air is pushed out from under the sucker, creating low pressure inside. The much higher atmospheric pressure outside pushes the sucker firmly against the surface.

ask_qa.q: What role does the Earth's rotation play in cyclones?
ask_qa.a: The Earth's rotation provides the 'spin' needed for the rising air to form a revolving system. Without rotation, the air would just move straight toward the low-pressure center.

ask_qa.q: What is the definition of pressure?
ask_qa.a: Pressure is defined as the force acting per unit area of a surface.

ask_qa.q: What is the formula for calculating pressure?
ask_qa.a: The formula for pressure is Pressure = Force / Area.

ask_qa.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
ask_qa.a: The SI unit of pressure is the Pascal (Pa), which is also written as Newton per square metre (N/m²).

ask_qa.q: Pressure kya hota hai?
ask_qa.a: Jab hum kisi area par force lagate hain, toh use pressure kehte hain. Iska formula Force divided by Area hai.

ask_qa.q: Why do school bags have broad straps?
ask_qa.a: Broad straps increase the surface area, which reduces the pressure on the shoulders, making the bag feel less heavy and more comfortable.

ask_qa.q: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one?
ask_qa.a: A sharp knife has a very small area at its edge, which creates high pressure even with little force, making it easier to cut.

ask_qa.q: Why is it difficult to carry a bucket with a thin handle?
ask_qa.a: A thin handle has a small area, which exerts more pressure on your hand, causing pain.

ask_qa.q: Why do porters put a round piece of cloth on their heads?
ask_qa.a: The cloth increases the area of contact for the heavy load, which reduces the pressure on their head.

ask_qa.q: How does liquid pressure change with depth?
ask_qa.a: Liquid pressure increases as the height (depth) of the liquid column increases.

ask_qa.q: Do liquids exert pressure on the walls of their container?
ask_qa.a: Yes, liquids exert pressure in all directions, including horizontally on the side walls of a container.

ask_qa.q: Why are water tanks kept at a height?
ask_qa.a: Tanks are placed at a height so that the tall water column creates enough pressure to ensure a strong stream of water in the taps below.

ask_qa.q: Why is the base of a dam made very thick and broad?
ask_qa.a: The base is broad to withstand the very high horizontal water pressure that occurs at the bottom of the dam.

ask_qa.q: What is atmospheric pressure?
ask_qa.a: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the envelope of air (atmosphere) surrounding the Earth on all objects.

ask_qa.q: Why are we not crushed by atmospheric pressure?
ask_qa.a: The pressure inside our bodies, caused by fluids and gases in our tissues, is equal to the atmospheric pressure and balances it out.

ask_qa.q: What causes wind to blow?
ask_qa.a: Wind is caused by the movement of air from a region of high pressure to a region of low pressure.

ask_qa.q: What is the relationship between wind speed and air pressure?
ask_qa.a: High-speed winds are accompanied by a reduction in air pressure in that area.

ask_qa.q: Why do roofs of houses sometimes blow off during a storm?
ask_qa.a: High-speed winds over the roof create low pressure, and if the pressure inside the house is higher, it can lift and blow the roof away.

ask_qa.q: How does warm air behave compared to cool air?
ask_qa.a: Warm air is lighter and rises, creating a low-pressure area, while cooler air is heavier and rushes in to fill that space.

ask_qa.q: What happens to a balloon when you blow air into it?
ask_qa.a: The air particles inside exert pressure in all directions on the walls of the balloon, causing it to inflate.

ask_qa.q: What is a storm?
ask_qa.a: A storm is a weather condition characterized by strong winds accompanied by rain, hail, or snow.

ask_qa.q: How do thunderstorms form?
ask_qa.a: They form when warm, moist air rises rapidly, cools, and condenses to form clouds, accompanied by strong upward and downward winds.

ask_qa.q: What causes lightning?
ask_qa.a: Lightning is caused by the buildup and sudden flow of electric charges between clouds or between a cloud and the ground.

ask_qa.q: What is thunder?
ask_qa.a: Thunder is the loud sound produced when lightning rapidly heats the surrounding air, causing it to expand explosively.

ask_qa.q: Why should we not stand under a tree during lightning?
ask_qa.a: Lightning tends to strike tall objects, and trees can be dangerous conductors that cause severe burns or death.

ask_qa.q: What is a lightning conductor?
ask_qa.a: It is a metallic rod installed on buildings that provides a safe path for electric charges to flow into the ground, protecting the structure.

ask_qa.q: What is a cyclone?
ask_qa.a: A cyclone is a massive spinning storm with a very low-pressure center that forms over warm ocean waters.

ask_qa.q: What is the 'eye' of a cyclone?
ask_qa.a: The 'eye' is the calm, low-pressure center of a cyclone where winds are light and there is no rain.

ask_qa.q: Why do cyclones lose strength over land?
ask_qa.a: Cyclones need warm, moist ocean air for energy; once they reach land, this moisture source is cut off and they weaken.

ask_qa.q: What is the unit 'millibar' used for?
ask_qa.a: Millibar (mb) is a practical unit of air pressure used in weather reporting, equal to 100 Pascals.

ask_qa.q: How does the IMD help with cyclones?
ask_qa.a: The India Meteorological Department monitors and tracks cyclones using satellites to issue warnings and alerts.

ask_qa.q: Why is it safer inside a car during lightning?
ask_qa.a: A car acts as a safe enclosure that can shield you from a direct lightning strike.

ask_qa.q: What are 'Mango Showers'?
ask_qa.a: These are local thunderstorms in Kerala and Karnataka that occur before the monsoon and help in ripening mangoes.

ask_qa.q: What causes the static charges in clouds?
ask_qa.a: Strong winds blowing ice particles and water droplets up and down rub against each other, creating electric charges.

ask_qa.q: Where are the positive and negative charges located in a cloud?
ask_qa.a: Positively charged ice particles move to the upper part of the cloud, while negatively charged water droplets occupy the lower part.

ask_qa.q: Define wind pressure.
ask_qa.a: Wind pressure is the force exerted by moving air on objects like fallen leaves, trees, or windows.

ask_qa.q: How does land breeze form?
ask_qa.a: At night, land cools faster than the sea. Air moves from the high-pressure land to the low-pressure sea, creating a land breeze.

ask_qa.q: How does sea breeze form?
ask_qa.a: During the day, land heats up faster than the sea. Air rises over land, and cool air from the high-pressure sea moves toward the land.

ask_qa.q: Why do banners have holes in them?
ask_qa.a: Holes allow air to pass through, reducing the wind pressure so the banner doesn't get torn or blown away by strong winds.

ask_qa.q: What is the effect of cyclone seawater on farmland?
ask_qa.a: Seawater can flood the land and the salt content makes the soil less fertile, damaging crops.

ask_qa.q: Calculate pressure if 100N force acts on 2 square metres.
ask_qa.a: Pressure = 100N / 2m² = 50 Pa.

ask_qa.q: Does the diameter of a pipe affect the pressure at the bottom?
ask_qa.a: No, liquid pressure depends on the height of the water column, not the diameter or weight of the water.

ask_qa.q: What should you do if you are in water during lightning?
ask_qa.a: You should immediately get out of the water as it can conduct electricity.

ask_qa.q: How high can a cyclone's wall of water be?
ask_qa.a: A cyclone can push a surge of water as high as 3 to 12 metres towards the shore.

ask_qa.q: What is the peak speed of the Amphan cyclone mentioned in the text?
ask_qa.a: The Amphan cyclone of 2020 reached peak wind speeds of 270 km/h.

ask_qa.q: Is air an electrical conductor or insulator?
ask_qa.a: Normally, air is an electrical insulator, but it breaks down when the build-up of electric charges in clouds becomes very large.

ask_qa.q: Why are windows kept open during storms?
ask_qa.a: Keeping windows open reduces the pressure difference between the inside and outside of the house, protecting the roof.

ask_qa.q: What is Kalboishakhi?
ask_qa.a: It is a local name for thunderstorms in West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand.

ask_qa.q: Why does a punctured bicycle tube collapse?
ask_qa.a: The air inside is at high pressure; when punctured, air rushes out to the low-pressure area outside, causing the tube to deflate.

ask_qa.q: If a force of 100 N is applied on a cardboard of area 2 m², what will be the pressure?
ask_qa.a: Using the formula Pressure = Force / Area, the calculation is 100 N / 2 m², which equals 50 N/m² or 50 Pa.

ask_qa.q: Calculate the pressure exerted by an elephant weighing 20,000 N standing on four feet, if each foot covers 0.25 m².
ask_qa.a: Total area = 4 × 0.25 m² = 1 m². Pressure = Force / Area = 20,000 N / 1 m² = 20,000 Pa.

ask_qa.q: Between two boats, Boat A (base 7 m², 5 people) and Boat B (base 3.5 m², 3 people), which experiences more pressure if each person weighs 700 N?
ask_qa.a: Pressure A = (5 × 700)/7 = 500 Pa. Pressure B = (3 × 700)/3.5 = 600 Pa. Boat B experiences 100 Pa more pressure than Boat A.

ask_qa.q: Give an example of how broad straps are used in daily life to reduce pressure.
ask_qa.a: School bags are made with broad straps to spread the weight over a larger shoulder area, making it more comfortable and reducing the pressure felt.

ask_qa.q: Why is it easier to drive a nail into wood using its pointed end rather than its head?
ask_qa.a: The pointed end has a very small area, which results in higher pressure for the same force, making it easier to penetrate the wood.

ask_qa.q: How can you use a blunt knife and a sharp knife to demonstrate the concept of area and pressure?
ask_qa.a: Cutting an apple with a sharp edge is easy because the small area creates high pressure; using the blunt edge is difficult because the larger area creates less pressure.

ask_qa.q: Give a real-life use of increasing area to carry heavy loads on the head.
ask_qa.a: Porters place a round piece of cloth on their heads to increase the area of contact, which reduces the pressure exerted by the heavy load.

ask_qa.q: Why are water tanks in a locality usually placed at a height?
ask_qa.a: Liquid pressure depends on the height of the water column; placing tanks high up increases the pressure to ensure a powerful stream of water in taps.

ask_qa.q: If two friends live on different floors (1st and 2nd) and the tank is on the top, who gets a more powerful water stream?
ask_qa.a: The friend on the 1st floor will get a more powerful stream because the height of the water column is greater for them, resulting in higher pressure.

ask_qa.q: How do dams withstand the horizontal pressure of water at the bottom?
ask_qa.a: The base of a dam is built much broader than the top to support the structure and withstand the high horizontal pressure found at greater depths.

ask_qa.q: What is a practical example showing that air exerts pressure in all directions?
ask_qa.a: When you blow air into a balloon, it inflates and expands in all directions, showing that air exerts pressure on all its internal walls.

ask_qa.q: How does a rubber sucker work when pressed against a smooth surface?
ask_qa.a: Air is pushed out from under the sucker, creating low pressure inside; the higher atmospheric pressure outside then pushes it firmly against the surface.

ask_qa.q: What is the force exerted by the atmosphere on a 15 cm × 15 cm area?
ask_qa.a: It is nearly equal to the force of gravity on an object of mass 225 kg, which is approximately 2250 N.

ask_qa.q: Why don't we get crushed by the massive weight of the atmosphere?
ask_qa.a: The pressure inside our bodies, caused by fluids and gases in tissues and organs, is equal to and balances the atmospheric pressure outside.

ask_qa.q: How do you express air pressure in hectopascals (hPa)?
ask_qa.a: One hectopascal (hPa) is equal to 100 Pascals (Pa).

ask_qa.q: What is the result of blowing air between two inflated balloons hung 6-10 cm apart?
ask_qa.a: The balloons move towards each other because the high-speed air between them creates a low-pressure area, and the higher surrounding pressure pushes them inward.

ask_qa.q: Give an example of how high-speed winds can damage a house.
ask_qa.a: High-speed winds create low pressure above a roof; if the roof is weak, the higher pressure from inside the house can lift it and blow it away.

ask_qa.q: Calculate the pressure in Pascals if a weather report says the air pressure is 10 millibars.
ask_qa.a: Since 1 millibar equals 100 Pa, a pressure of 10 millibars is equal to 1,000 Pa.

ask_qa.q: What causes the 'Mango Showers' in Kerala and Karnataka?
ask_qa.a: They are caused by local thunderstorms that occur before the monsoon, providing the moisture and conditions needed to ripen mangoes.

ask_qa.q: What happens when you blow over a strip of paper held between your fingers?
ask_qa.a: The paper rises because blowing air over the top creates high-speed winds and low pressure, allowing the higher pressure below to push it up.

ask_qa.q: Where should you go for safety during lightning if you are outdoors?
ask_qa.a: Find a low-lying open area and crouch down in the 'safe position' while staying away from tall objects like trees.

ask_qa.q: How does a lightning conductor protect a building?
ask_qa.a: It is a metallic rod with a pointed end that provides an easy, safe path for electric charges to flow from the clouds into the ground.

ask_qa.q: What was the peak wind speed of the Amphan cyclone in 2020?
ask_qa.a: The Amphan cyclone had peak wind speeds of 270 km/h.

ask_qa.q: How high can the wall of water pushed by a cyclone surge reach?
ask_qa.a: A cyclone can push a surge of water as high as 3 to 12 metres towards the shore.

ask_qa.q: What real-life effect does seawater flooding have on farmland after a cyclone?
ask_qa.a: The salt in the seawater contaminates the soil and makes it less fertile, which damages crops for a long time.

ask_qa.q: Why are holes made in banners and hoardings?
ask_qa.a: Holes allow air to pass through, which reduces the force and pressure exerted by wind so the banners don't get torn or blown down.

ask_qa.q: Explain what happens when an inflated balloon's mouth is left open.
ask_qa.a: Air moves from the high-pressure region inside the balloon to the low-pressure region outside until the pressure is equalized.

ask_qa.q: What is the relationship between wind speed and pressure difference?
ask_qa.a: The speed of the wind or escaping air is higher if the pressure difference between the two regions is higher.

ask_qa.q: What happens to the pressure at the bottom of a pipe if you add more water?
ask_qa.a: As the height of the water column increases, the pressure at the bottom also increases, causing a balloon attached there to bulge more.

ask_qa.q: How does the Earth's rotation affect moving air during a cyclone?
ask_qa.a: Earth's rotation causes the rising, moving air to spin, creating a rotating system of clouds and winds around a low-pressure eye.

ask_qa.q: What is the main difference between how narrow straps and broad straps exert pressure?
ask_qa.a: Narrow straps have a smaller area, concentrating the force and creating high pressure that hurts the shoulders. Broad straps spread the same force over a larger area, reducing the pressure and making the bag comfortable.

ask_qa.q: Is it true that the total weight of water in a pipe determines the pressure at the bottom?
ask_qa.a: No, this is a common misconception. Liquid pressure depends on the height of the water column, not the diameter of the pipe or the total weight of the water.

ask_qa.q: Why does a sharp knife cut easier than a blunt one if the applied force is the same?
ask_qa.a: A sharp knife has a much smaller surface area at its edge. Since pressure is force divided by area, the smaller area produces a much higher pressure, which slices through objects easily.

ask_qa.q: Why don't we feel the massive weight of atmospheric pressure pushing down on us?
ask_qa.a: We aren't crushed because the pressure inside our bodies, caused by fluids and gases in our tissues and organs, balances the outside atmospheric pressure.

ask_qa.q: Is it true that air moves from low pressure to high pressure?
ask_qa.a: No, it is the opposite. Air always moves from a region of high pressure to a region of low pressure, which is what creates wind.

ask_qa.q: What is the difference between a regular storm and a thunderstorm?
ask_qa.a: A storm is simply strong winds with rain, hail, or snow. A thunderstorm specifically includes lightning and the loud sound of thunder caused by electrical charges.

ask_qa.q: Does high-speed wind increase or decrease air pressure?
ask_qa.a: High-speed winds are always accompanied by a reduction in air pressure in that specific area.

ask_qa.q: Why do some people think you should close all windows during a storm, and why is that wrong?
ask_qa.a: People think it keeps wind out, but it actually creates a large pressure difference between the high pressure inside and low pressure outside. Keeping windows open equalizes the pressure so the roof doesn't blow off.

ask_qa.q: What is the 'eye' of a cyclone, and is it the most violent part?
ask_qa.a: The eye is the calm, low-pressure center of the cyclone with light winds and no rain. The most violent winds and heavy rains actually occur in the region surrounding the eye.

ask_qa.q: Is it true that cyclones can form anywhere on Earth?
ask_qa.a: No, cyclones specifically form over warm ocean waters where moist air can rise and the Earth's rotation can cause the system to spin.

ask_qa.q: What is the difference between sea breeze and land breeze?
ask_qa.a: Sea breeze occurs during the day when air moves from the sea to the land. Land breeze occurs at night when air moves from the cooler land toward the warmer sea.

ask_qa.q: Why do porters use a round piece of cloth on their heads for heavy loads?
ask_qa.a: The cloth increases the area of contact between the load and the head. By increasing the area, the pressure on the head is reduced, making the weight easier to bear.

ask_qa.q: How does liquid pressure change as you go deeper into a tank?
ask_qa.a: Liquid pressure increases as the height of the liquid column (depth) increases. This is why dams are built with a broader base at the bottom.

ask_qa.q: Can a rubber sucker stick to a rough brick wall?
ask_qa.a: No, it needs a smooth, flat surface. On a rough surface, air can leak back in, preventing the pressure difference needed for atmospheric pressure to hold the sucker in place.

ask_qa.q: What would happen to cyclones if the Earth stopped rotating?
ask_qa.a: If the Earth stopped rotating, cyclones would not form because the rotation is what provides the 'spin' to the rising air system.

ask_qa.q: Is air a conductor of electricity?
ask_qa.a: Normally, air is an electrical insulator. However, during a storm, when the build-up of charges in clouds becomes very large, the insulating property breaks down and electricity flows as lightning.

ask_qa.q: Why do banner makers put holes in large hoardings?
ask_qa.a: Holes allow air to pass through the banner. This reduces the wind pressure exerted on the surface so the banner doesn't get torn or blown down by strong winds.

ask_qa.q: What is the difference between how positive and negative charges are arranged in a storm cloud?
ask_qa.a: Positively charged lighter ice particles move to the upper part of the cloud, while negatively charged heavier water droplets stay in the lower part.

ask_qa.q: Why does a balloon expand in all directions when you blow into it?
ask_qa.a: This happens because air is a gas, and gases exert pressure in all directions on the walls of their container.

ask_qa.q: Does a cyclone get stronger or weaker when it hits land?
ask_qa.a: It loses strength because it is cut off from its source of energy—the warm, moist air over the ocean.

ask_qa.q: Why is it safer to stay in a car than under a tree during lightning?
ask_qa.a: Lightning strikes tall objects like trees. A car acts as a safe enclosure that can shield you from the electricity if it strikes nearby.

ask_qa.q: Is the Pascal (Pa) different from N/m²?
ask_qa.a: No, they are the same thing. One Pascal is equal to one Newton per square metre (1 N/m²).

ask_qa.q: Why do water tanks need to be high up to work for a ground-floor tap?
ask_qa.a: The height creates a tall water column, which results in higher pressure at the bottom, ensuring a strong flow of water from the tap.

ask_qa.q: How does the 'Mango Shower' help farmers?
ask_qa.a: These are local thunderstorms in South India that occur before the monsoon and provide the necessary moisture for mangoes to ripen.

ask_qa.q: What is the difference between Kalboishakhi and Bordoisila?
ask_qa.a: They are local names for similar thunderstorms; Kalboishakhi is used in West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand, while Bordoisila is used in Assam.

ask_qa.q: If two vessels have different shapes but the same water level, is the pressure at the bottom different?
ask_qa.a: No, the pressure at the bottom will be equal in both vessels as long as the height of the water column is the same.

ask_qa.q: Why shouldn't you use an umbrella with a metal rod during a thunderstorm?
ask_qa.a: Metal is a good conductor of electricity. Since lightning is a flow of electric charges, a metallic rod can attract the strike and cause severe harm.

ask_qa.q: What creates the loud sound of thunder?
ask_qa.a: Lightning rapidly heats the air, causing it to expand suddenly and explosively, which produces the sound wave we hear as thunder.

ask_qa.q: Is the weight of the air column over a small area really that heavy?
ask_qa.a: Yes, the force on an area of 15 cm x 15 cm is nearly equal to the weight of a 225 kg mass, but we don't feel it because of internal body pressure.

ask_qa.q: What determines the speed of wind between two areas?
ask_qa.a: The wind speed depends on the pressure difference; the higher the pressure difference between two regions, the faster the air will move.

ask_qa.q: Pressure kya hai simple words mein?
ask_qa.a: Jab hum kisi surface ke ek area par force lagate hain, use pressure kehte hain. Iska formula hai: Pressure = Force / Area.

ask_qa.q: Pressure ki unit kya hoti hai?
ask_qa.a: Pressure ki SI unit Pascal (Pa) hai, jise hum Newton per square metre (N/m²) bhi kehte hain.

ask_qa.q: Sharp knife se apple katna easy kyu hota hai?
ask_qa.a: Sharp edge ka area bahut kam hota hai, jiski wajah se pressure badh jata hai aur apple aasani se kat jata hai.

ask_qa.q: School bag ke straps broad kyu hote hain?
ask_qa.a: Broad straps area badha dete hain, jisse shoulders par pressure kam ho jata hai aur bag uthana comfortable hota hai.

ask_qa.q: Porters apne sar par kapda kyu rakhte hain jab load uthate hain?
ask_qa.a: Round kapda rakhne se weight ke contact ka area badh jata hai, jisse unke sar par pressure kam parta hai.

ask_qa.q: Water tanks ko hamesha height par kyu rakhte hain?
ask_qa.a: Height badhne se water column ka pressure badh jata hai, jisse taps mein paani ka flow tez aata hai.

ask_qa.q: Kya liquids walls par bhi pressure lagate hain?
ask_qa.a: Haan, liquids aur gases apne container ki walls par har direction mein pressure exert karte hain.

ask_qa.q: Dams ka base itna thick aur broad kyu banate hain?
ask_qa.a: Kyuki bottom par paani ka horizontal pressure bahut zyada hota hai, use jhelne ke liye base ko broad banaya jata hai.

ask_qa.q: Atmospheric pressure kya hai?
ask_qa.a: Hamare charo taraf jo hawa ka envelope (atmosphere) hai, wo har cheez par pressure lagata hai, jise atmospheric pressure kehte hain.

ask_qa.q: Itni bhari hawa humein crush kyu nahi kar deti?
ask_qa.a: Hamari body ke andar ka fluids aur gases ka pressure bahar ke atmospheric pressure ke barabar hota hai, isliye wo balance ho jata hai.

ask_qa.q: Rubber sucker wall se kyu chipak jata hai?
ask_qa.a: Press karne par sucker ke andar ki hawa nikal jati hai. Bahar ka high atmospheric pressure use wall se chipka kar rakhta hai.

ask_qa.q: Hawa (Wind) kyu chalti hai?
ask_qa.a: Jab hawa high pressure wale area se low pressure wale area ki taraf move karti hai, toh wind banti hai.

ask_qa.q: Wind speed aur pressure ka kya lena-dena hai?
ask_qa.a: Jab wind ki speed bahut fast hoti hai, toh wahan ka air pressure kam (reduce) ho jata hai.

ask_qa.q: Fast wind mein gharon ki chhat (roofs) kyu udd jati hain?
ask_qa.a: Chhat ke upar fast hawa se low pressure banta hai. Agar andar ka pressure zyada ho, toh wo roof ko lift karke uda deta hai.

ask_qa.q: Storm ke time windows khuli rakhna kyu safe hai?
ask_qa.a: Windows khuli rakhne se ghar ke andar aur bahar ka pressure balance ho jata hai, jisse roof udne ka khatra kam ho jata hai.

ask_qa.q: Garm hawa (Warm air) upar kyu uthti hai?
ask_qa.a: Warm air thandi hawa se halki hoti hai, isliye wo upar uthti hai aur niche low pressure area banati hai.

ask_qa.q: Sea Breeze kya hoti hai?
ask_qa.a: Din mein land jaldi garm hoti hai aur hawa upar uthti hai. Tab sea se thandi hawa land ki taraf aati hai, jise sea breeze kehte hain.

ask_qa.q: Thunderstorm kaise banta hai?
ask_qa.a: Jab garm aur moist hawa tezi se upar uthti hai, wo thandi hokar clouds banati hai aur baarish ke saath bijli kadakti hai.

ask_qa.q: Clouds mein bijli (Lightning) kaise paida hoti hai?
ask_qa.a: Strong winds ki wajah se ice particles aur water droplets aapas mein rub karte hain, jisse clouds mein static electric charges ban jaate hain.

ask_qa.q: Thunder kyu sunayi deti hai?
ask_qa.a: Lightning hawa ko bahut tezi se garm karti hai, jisse hawa dhamake ke saath expand hoti hai aur loud sound paida karti hai.

ask_qa.q: Lightning ke time ped (tree) ke niche kyu nahi khade hona chahiye?
ask_qa.a: Lightning tall objects par jaldi strike karti hai, isliye ped ke niche rehna dangerous hai aur jaan ja sakti hai.

ask_qa.q: Lightning conductor kya kaam karta hai?
ask_qa.a: Ye building par laga ek metallic rod hota hai jo bijli ke jhatke ko safely zameen (ground) ke andar bhej deta hai.

ask_qa.q: Cyclone kya hai?
ask_qa.a: Ye ek massive spinning storm hai jo warm ocean waters ke upar banta hai aur iska center low pressure hota hai.

ask_qa.q: Cyclone ki 'Eye' kya hoti hai?
ask_qa.a: Cyclone ke bilkul center ko 'Eye' kehte hain, jahan hawa ekdum shaant hoti hai aur koi baarish nahi hoti.

ask_qa.q: Zameen (land) par aate hi cyclone kamzor kyu ho jata hai?
ask_qa.a: Cyclone ko energy ocean ki moist hawa se milti hai. Land par aate hi ye moisture khatam ho jata hai, isliye wo thanda pad jata hai.

ask_qa.q: Cyclone se kheti (farmland) ko kya nuksan hota hai?
ask_qa.a: Samundar ka namkeen paani khet mein bhar jata hai, jo mitti ko less fertile bana deta hai aur crops kharab ho jati hain.

ask_qa.q: IMD humein cyclone se kaise bachata hai?
ask_qa.a: India Meteorological Department satellites se cyclone ko track karta hai aur timely warnings deta hai taaki log safe jagah ja sakein.

ask_qa.q: Holes banners aur hoardings mein kyu kiye jaate hain?
ask_qa.a: Holes se hawa pass ho jati hai, jisse banner par wind pressure kam parta hai aur wo phatne se bach jata hai.

ask_qa.q: Bicycle tube puncture hone par pichak kyu jata hai?
ask_qa.a: Andar ki high pressure hawa puncture se bahar nikal jati hai taaki wo low pressure bahar ke saath barabar ho sake.

ask_qa.q: Agar 100N force 2m² area par lage toh pressure kitna hoga?
ask_qa.a: Pressure = 100 / 2 = 50 Pascal (Pa).

ask_qa.q: What is the mathematical formula for Pressure?
ask_qa.a: The formula for pressure is Pressure = Force / Area.

ask_qa.q: What does the symbol 'Pa' stand for?
ask_qa.a: The symbol Pa stands for Pascal, the SI unit of pressure named after a scientist.

ask_qa.q: Define Atmospheric Pressure.
ask_qa.a: Atmospheric pressure is the pressure exerted by the envelope of air (the atmosphere) that surrounds the Earth on all objects.

ask_qa.q: What is Wind?
ask_qa.a: Wind is the movement of air from a region of high air pressure to a region of low air pressure.

ask_qa.q: What is Wind Pressure?
ask_qa.a: Wind pressure is the force exerted by moving air on objects, such as when it sways trees or rattles windows.

ask_qa.q: Define a Thunderstorm.
ask_qa.a: A thunderstorm is a storm characterized by the presence of lightning and the loud sound of thunder.

ask_qa.q: What is Lightning?
ask_qa.a: Lightning is a sudden flow of electric charges between clouds, within a cloud, or between a cloud and the ground, producing a bright flash of light.

ask_qa.q: Define the Atmosphere.
ask_qa.a: The atmosphere is the envelope of air surrounding the Earth, containing gases like nitrogen, oxygen, and carbon dioxide.

ask_qa.q: What are Kalboishakhi and Bordoisila?
ask_qa.a: These are local names for thunderstorms in West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand (Kalboishakhi) and Assam (Bordoisila).

ask_qa.q: What is the unit 'millibar' (mb)?
ask_qa.a: The millibar is a practical unit of air pressure equal to 100 Pascals, often used in weather reporting.

ask_qa.q: What is a Hectopascal (hPa)?
ask_qa.a: A hectopascal is a unit of pressure equal to 100 Pascals.

ask_qa.q: Define Sea Breeze.
ask_qa.a: Sea breeze is the movement of cool air from the sea toward the land during the day when the land is at lower pressure.

ask_qa.q: Define Land Breeze.
ask_qa.a: Land breeze is the movement of air from the land toward the sea at night when the sea is at lower pressure.

ask_qa.q: What is 'IMD'?
ask_qa.a: IMD stands for the India Meteorological Department, which monitors cyclones and thunderstorms using satellites.

ask_qa.q: What are Static Electric Charges in the context of clouds?
ask_qa.a: These are charges created by the rubbing of ice particles and water droplets moving up and down within clouds during a storm.

ask_qa.q: What does a high-pressure region mean?
ask_qa.a: A high-pressure region is an area where the air or liquid exerts a greater force on its surroundings compared to neighboring areas.

ask_qa.q: What does a low-pressure region mean?
ask_qa.a: A low-pressure region is an area where the force per unit area is reduced, often caused by warm air rising.

ask_qa.q: How do liquids exert pressure?
ask_qa.a: Liquids exert pressure in all directions, both vertically on the bottom and horizontally on the walls of their container.

ask_qa.q: What is the effect of height on liquid pressure?
ask_qa.a: Liquid pressure increases as the height of the liquid column (the depth) increases.

ask_qa.q: Pressure ka simple meaning kya hai?
ask_qa.a: Pressure ka matlab hai force per unit area. Agar force same ho lekin area chhota ho, toh pressure zyada lagta hai.

ask_qa.q: What is the 'Pascal' in short form?
ask_qa.a: The short form or symbol for Pascal is 'Pa'.

ask_qa.q: Why does a school bag with broad straps feel more comfortable than one with narrow straps?
ask_qa.a: Broad straps spread the weight of the bag over a larger area of the shoulders, which reduces the pressure. Narrow straps focus the weight on a smaller area, causing higher pressure and pain.

ask_qa.q: How does the pointed end of a nail make it easier to drive into a surface?
ask_qa.a: The pointed end has a very small area, which results in much higher pressure for the same amount of force, allowing it to pierce the surface easily.

ask_qa.q: Why do porters place a round piece of cloth on their heads when carrying heavy loads?
ask_qa.a: The cloth increases the area of contact between the load and their head, which reduces the pressure exerted by the heavy weight.

ask_qa.q: How does increasing the height of a liquid column affect pressure?
ask_qa.a: As the height of the liquid column increases, the pressure at the bottom also increases. This is why a taller column of water creates a bigger bulge in a balloon.

ask_qa.q: Why are overhead water tanks always placed at a height?
ask_qa.a: Placing tanks at a height increases the pressure in the taps due to the tall water column, resulting in a more powerful stream of water.

ask_qa.q: Why is the base of a dam built much broader than the top?
ask_qa.a: A broad base helps the dam withstand the very high horizontal water pressure that occurs near the bottom of the structure.

ask_qa.q: How does air exert pressure on objects like a chart paper sheet?
ask_qa.a: The atmosphere is an envelope of air that exerts force on surfaces; as the area of the surface increases, the total force exerted by the air also increases.

ask_qa.q: Why does a balloon expand in all directions when you blow air into it?
ask_qa.a: This happens because the air being filled inside the balloon exerts pressure in all directions against its walls.

ask_qa.q: How does a rubber sucker stick to a smooth surface?
ask_qa.a: Pressing the sucker pushes the air out from inside, creating low pressure. The higher atmospheric pressure outside then pushes the sucker firmly against the surface.

ask_qa.q: Why are humans not crushed by the heavy weight of atmospheric pressure?
ask_qa.a: The pressure inside our bodies, caused by fluids and gases in our tissues, is equal to the atmospheric pressure and balances it from the inside.

ask_qa.q: What causes wind to move between two regions?
ask_qa.a: Air moves when there is a pressure difference; it always flows from a region of high pressure to a region of low pressure.

ask_qa.q: How does a sea breeze form during the day?
ask_qa.a: Land heats up faster than water, causing warm air to rise and create low pressure. Cool air from the high-pressure sea then rushes in toward the land.

ask_qa.q: What happens to air pressure when wind speed increases?
ask_qa.a: High-speed winds are accompanied by a reduction in air pressure in that specific area.

ask_qa.q: Why do the roofs of houses sometimes blow off during high-speed storms?
ask_qa.a: High-speed winds create low pressure over the roof. If the pressure inside the house is higher, the force can lift and blow the roof away.

ask_qa.q: Why is it safer to keep windows open during a storm with high-speed winds?
ask_qa.a: Open windows allow the air to flow through, reducing the pressure difference between the inside and outside of the house and protecting the roof.

ask_qa.q: How does warm air rising lead to the formation of clouds?
ask_qa.a: As warm air rises, it expands and cools, causing the moisture inside it to condense into water droplets that form clouds.

ask_qa.q: What causes the rubbing that creates static electric charges in clouds?
ask_qa.a: Strong winds blowing ice particles and water droplets upwards and downwards cause them to rub against each other, creating electric charges.

ask_qa.q: How do charges separate within a thunderstorm cloud?
ask_qa.a: Lighter, positively charged ice particles move to the upper part of the cloud, while heavier, negatively charged water droplets occupy the lower part.

ask_qa.q: What causes the bright flash of light known as lightning?
ask_qa.a: When the build-up of charges becomes very large, the air's insulation breaks down, leading to a sudden flow of electricity between clouds or the ground.

ask_qa.q: How is thunder produced during a storm?
ask_qa.a: Lightning rapidly heats the surrounding air, causing it to expand explosively and create a loud sound wave.

ask_qa.q: Why are lightning conductors used on tall buildings?
ask_qa.a: They provide a safe, easy metallic path for electric charges to flow from the sky into the ground, protecting the building from damage.

ask_qa.q: How does a cyclone begin to form over the ocean?
ask_qa.a: Warm, moist air rises over the ocean and condenses, releasing heat back into the atmosphere. This makes the air rise more, creating a very low-pressure center.

ask_qa.q: Why do cyclones lose their strength once they reach land?
ask_qa.a: Cyclones get their energy from warm, moist ocean air; once they move over land, they are cut off from this moisture source and weaken.

ask_qa.q: How does a cyclone cause flooding in coastal areas?
ask_qa.a: Strong winds push ocean water toward the shore, creating a massive wall of water (surge) that can be 3–12 metres high.

ask_qa.q: Why does seawater flooding damage farmland?
ask_qa.a: The salt in the seawater makes the soil less fertile and can contaminate drinking water sources.

ask_qa.q: What causes air to escape from a balloon when the mouth is left open?
ask_qa.a: The air pressure inside the inflated balloon is higher than the pressure outside, so air moves from the high-pressure region to the low-pressure region.

ask_qa.q: How does air pressure inside a bicycle tube change when it gets punctured?
ask_qa.a: The high-pressure air inside escapes to the lower-pressure atmosphere outside, causing the tube to collapse.

ask_qa.q: Why do local thunderstorms help crops in some parts of India?
ask_qa.a: Storms like 'Mango Showers' provide necessary moisture before the monsoon, supporting the ripening of fruits and growth of crops like coffee.

ask_qa.q: What determines whether an object will sink in loose sand or stay on top?
ask_qa.a: It depends on pressure, not just weight. If a person stands vertically, their weight acts on a small area (feet), creating high pressure and making them sink; lying down spreads the weight over a large area, reducing pressure.

ask_qa.q: Why doesn't the total volume of water in a tank matter for tap pressure?
ask_qa.a: Liquid pressure depends only on the height of the water column above the tap. A very wide tank and a narrow pipe will exert the same pressure at the bottom if the water levels are at the same height.

ask_qa.q: How do porters use the concept of 'Area' to make their work easier?
ask_qa.a: Porters place a round piece of cloth on their heads to increase the area of contact with the heavy load. This reduces the pressure on their skull, making it easier to carry.

ask_qa.q: Why is the base of a dam made wider than the top?
ask_qa.a: Water pressure increases with depth and acts horizontally against the walls. A broad base is needed to withstand the massive pressure at the bottom of the reservoir.

ask_qa.q: If air pressure is so strong, why don't we feel it on our skin?
ask_qa.a: We don't feel it because the fluids and gases inside our bodies exert an equal outward pressure. This perfectly balances the atmospheric pressure pushing inward.

ask_qa.q: What would happen to the wind if the entire Earth was at the same temperature?
ask_qa.a: Wind is caused by pressure differences created by uneven heating. If temperatures were identical everywhere, there would be no pressure differences and the air would remain calm.

ask_qa.q: Why is it dangerous to hold a metallic umbrella during a thunderstorm?
ask_qa.a: Metal is a good conductor of electricity. Since lightning is a flow of electric charges, it can easily travel through the metal rod and cause a severe electric shock or death.

ask_qa.q: How does blowing over a strip of paper make it lift upward?
ask_qa.a: Blowing creates high-speed air over the paper, which reduces the air pressure on top. The higher atmospheric pressure underneath then pushes the paper up.

ask_qa.q: Why should we not stay in water (like a pool or sea) during lightning?
ask_qa.a: Water is an excellent conductor of electricity. If lightning strikes the water even at a distance, the charge can travel through the water and reach you instantly.

ask_qa.q: What provides the 'energy' for a cyclone to grow?
ask_qa.a: The energy comes from the heat released when water vapour condenses into rain. This heat warms the air further, causing it to rise faster and drop the pressure even more.

ask_qa.q: Why do cyclones dissipate (die out) shortly after hitting land?
ask_qa.a: Cyclones need a constant supply of warm, moist air from the ocean to keep going. Once they move over land, this moisture source is cut off, and they lose their energy.

ask_qa.q: How does a lightning conductor protect a skyscraper?
ask_qa.a: It is a tall metal rod that provides a low-resistance path for the electrical charge to flow directly into the ground, bypassing the building's structure.

ask_qa.q: Why are holes made in large banners and hoardings hanging across streets?
ask_qa.a: Holes allow air to pass through instead of hitting a solid surface. This reduces the wind pressure exerted on the banner so it doesn't tear or fall down.

ask_qa.q: What causes the 'spin' in a cyclone?
ask_qa.a: The spin is caused by the Earth's rotation. As air rushes toward the low-pressure center, the rotation of the planet deflects it, creating a spinning system.

ask_qa.q: What is the 'eye' of the cyclone like compared to the rest of the storm?
ask_qa.a: The eye is the central point of lowest pressure and is surprisingly calm with light winds and no rain, while the 'eye wall' surrounding it has the most violent winds.

ask_qa.q: How do 'Mango Showers' differ from regular monsoon rains?
ask_qa.a: Mango Showers are local thunderstorms that occur before the actual monsoon arrives. They are caused by local heating and help in the ripening of crops in South India.

ask_qa.q: Why does a rubber sucker stick better to a glass window than a wooden door?
ask_qa.a: Glass is perfectly smooth, allowing a vacuum to form when air is pushed out. Wood is porous or rough, letting air leak back in and equalizing the pressure.

ask_qa.q: Why does air rush out of a punctured bicycle tube?
ask_qa.a: The air inside the tube is compressed (high pressure). When a hole appears, the air naturally moves toward the lower atmospheric pressure outside.

ask_qa.q: How is the sound of thunder created?
ask_qa.a: Lightning heats the air to extreme temperatures instantly. This causes the air to expand explosively, creating a shockwave that we hear as a loud bang.

ask_qa.q: Why do we use sharp knives to cut vegetables instead of blunt ones?
ask_qa.a: A sharp knife has a tiny area at the edge. Since Pressure = Force / Area, a smaller area produces much higher pressure, allowing it to slice through skin easily.

ask_qa.q: Why is it safer to be inside a car during a storm than under a tree?
ask_qa.a: Lightning strikes tall, isolated objects like trees. A car acts as a metal cage that can shield you by conducting the electricity around the outside of the vehicle to the ground.

ask_qa.q: What happens to the pressure at the bottom of a container if you double the water height?
ask_qa.a: The pressure at the bottom will double because liquid pressure is directly proportional to the height of the liquid column.

ask_qa.q: In a storm, why might a roof lift off even if the wind is only blowing sideways?
ask_qa.a: Fast air moving over the roof creates low pressure above it. If windows are closed, the high-pressure air trapped inside the house pushes the roof upward.

ask_qa.q: Why are the straps of school bags made broad?
ask_qa.a: Broad straps increase the surface area over which the weight of the bag acts. This reduces the pressure on the student's shoulders, making it more comfortable.

ask_qa.q: Does air exert pressure only downwards?
ask_qa.a: No, like liquids, air exerts pressure in all directions—upwards, downwards, and sideways. This is why a balloon expands in every direction when inflated.

ask_qa.q: How does temperature affect the density of air?
ask_qa.a: When air is heated, it expands and becomes less dense (lighter). This causes it to rise, which is why warm air creates low-pressure regions.

ask_qa.q: What is the difference between land breeze and sea breeze timing?
ask_qa.a: Sea breeze occurs during the day when the land is hotter than the sea. Land breeze occurs at night when the sea is warmer than the land.

ask_qa.q: What unit do meteorologists use to measure air pressure?
ask_qa.a: While the SI unit is the Pascal (Pa), weather reports often use millibars (mb) or hectopascals (hPa). 1 mb = 100 Pa.

ask_qa.q: Why do positive and negative charges separate in a cloud?
ask_qa.a: Strong upward and downward winds cause ice particles and water droplets to rub against each other. Lighter ice particles (positive) move up, while heavier droplets (negative) stay lower.

ask_qa.q: How does the IMD track cyclones before they hit the coast?
ask_qa.a: The India Meteorological Department uses weather satellites and radar to monitor cloud patterns and wind speeds to predict the cyclone's path.

ask_qa.q: Why should you crouch low in an open field during lightning?
ask_qa.a: Lightning seeks the highest point to reach the ground. By crouching low, you reduce your height and the chance of being the primary target for a strike.

ask_qa.q: What is the 'surge' caused by a cyclone?
ask_qa.a: A surge is a wall of seawater (3–12 meters high) pushed toward the shore by the cyclone's powerful winds, causing massive coastal flooding.

ask_qa.q: Why does seawater flooding damage farmland for years?
ask_qa.a: Seawater is salty. When it floods land, the salt stays in the soil, making it infertile and killing crops that cannot grow in salty conditions.

ask_qa.q: How does air act as an insulator in a storm?
ask_qa.a: Normally, air prevents electricity from jumping between charges. Lightning only occurs when the charge build-up is so huge that the air's 'insulating' power finally fails.

ask_qa.q: Why is liquid pressure the same at the same depth in two different shaped bottles?
ask_qa.a: Liquid pressure only depends on the vertical height of the liquid column. The shape or width of the bottle does not change the pressure at a specific depth.

ask_qa.q: Why is it difficult to pull a rubber sucker off a smooth surface?
ask_qa.a: Because there is almost no air inside to push back, the full weight of the atmospheric pressure outside is pinning the sucker against the surface.

ask_qa.q: Why do we say 'High-speed winds result in lowering of air pressure'?
ask_qa.a: This is a scientific principle where the faster air moves, the less pressure it exerts on the surface below it. It's the reason why roofs fly off and paper lifts up.

ask_qa.q: What happens to the pressure if we apply the same force to half the area?
ask_qa.a: The pressure will double. Since Pressure = Force / Area, reducing the area by half makes the pressure twice as strong.

Thunderstorms have different local names in India, like 'Kalboishakhi' in West Bengal and 'Bordoisila' in Assam.

chapter.title: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents, and Solutions
chapter.summary: This chapter explores the science of how substances mix and why objects behave differently in liquids. You will learn the difference between uniform solutions and non-uniform mixtures, and how temperature affects how much a liquid can dissolve. Finally, it explains the concept of density and the displacement method used to measure the volume of irregular objects.
key_points: A solution is a uniform mixture of a solute (the part that dissolves) and a solvent (the part that does the dissolving).
In liquid-liquid solutions, the substance in the smaller amount is the solute.
A saturated solution cannot dissolve any more solute at its current temperature.
Solubility of most solids increases with temperature, while the solubility of gases decreases.
Density is defined as mass per unit volume (Density = Mass / Volume).
The SI unit for density is kg/m³, but g/mL or g/cm³ are also commonly used.
Relative density compares a substance's density to water and has no units.
Objects float if they are less dense than the liquid they are placed in.
The volume of irregular solids is measured by how much water they displace in a measuring cylinder.
Heating a substance usually increases its volume and decreases its density.
Mass is the quantity of matter, while weight is the force of gravity acting on it.
A meniscus is the curved surface of a liquid; read the bottom of it for clear liquids like water.

your homemade ORS tastes the same, no matter how much you drink. Why does it not taste salty in one sip and sweet in another? This is because when you add sugar and salt to water, they form a mixture in which the components are evenly distributed throughout. Can you predict whether this mixture is uniform or not (Fig. 9.1)? What happens when chalk powder is mixed with water—does it form a uniform mixture? When salt and sugar are mixed with water, a uniform mixture is formed, whereas when chalk powder or sand, or sawdust is mixed with water, the components are not evenly distributed. Such mixtures are known as non-uniform mixtures (Fig. 9.2a and 9.2b). Let us explore the science of mixing things together.
9.1 What Are Solute, Solvent, and Solution?

A uniform mixture, such as that of salt or sugar, and water, is called a solution. Whenever a solid is mixed with a liquid to form a solution, the solid component is called the solute, and the liquid component is called the solvent. The solute dissolves in the solvent to form a solution (Fig. 9.3). Solute + Solvent  Solution When a solution is formed by mixing two liquids, it is not always clear which substance is dissolving the other. In such cases, the substance present in smaller amount is called the solute, while the one in larger amount is called the solvent.

9.2  How Much Solute Can a Fixed Amount of

Some discussion points
z How many spoons of salt were you able to dissolve before

z What does this indicate about the capacity of water to
dissolve salt? What will happen if we keep on adding more salt in a given amount of water?

You might have observed that, initially, the salt completely dissolves in the water, forming a solution. After adding a few more spoons of salt, a stage comes when the added salt does not dissolve completely and the undissolved salt settles at the bottom. This indicates that the water can no longer dissolve any more salt because it has reached its limit. The solution in which more solute can be dissolved at a given temperature, is called an unsaturated solution (Fig. 9.5). However, when the solute stops dissolving and begins to settle at the bottom, the solution is called a saturated solution at that particular temperature (Fig. 9.6). The amount of solute present in a fixed quantity of solution (or solvent) is termed as its concentration . Depending upon the amount of solute present in a fixed quantity of solution, it can be called a dilute solution (less amount of solute) or a concentrated solution (more amount of solute). Dilute and concentrated are relative terms. So, one can say in Activity 9.1, the solution obtained by dissolving one spoon of salt is dilute as compared to that obtained by dissolving two or more spoons of salt. Can you now reflect — which solution is more concentrated; 2 spoons of salt in 100 mL of water or 4 spoons of salt in 50 mL of water? We can say that the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a fixed quantity of the solvent is called its solubility. Does temperature affect the solubility of a solute? Let us find out!

solute?

It has been found that for most of the substances, the solubility increases with an increase in temperature. We can also say that a saturated solution at a particular temperature behaves as an unsaturated solution if the temperature is increased.
Our scientific heritage

Water has primarily been used as a solvent for the preparation of medicinal formulations in Ayurveda, Siddha, and other traditional systems of medicine in India. Additionally, drug formulations have been prepared using hydro-alcoholic extracts of the herbs. The Indian systems of medicine have also referred to the use of oils, ghee, milk, and other substances as solvents for drug formulations, to help achieve the therapeutic benefits of the drug.

She earned a Doctorate of Science, becoming the second Indian woman to do so after Janaki Ammal. Do gases also dissolve in water?
9.3  Solubility of Gases

Many gases, including oxygen, dissolve in water. Oxygen dissolves in water only to a small extent. Even though present in minute quantities, it is this dissolved oxygen that sustains all aquatic life, including plants, fishes, and other organisms. Is the mixture of gases in water a uniform or non-uniform mixture? It is a uniform mixture because the gases dissolve evenly in water. Does temperature affect the solubility of gases in liquids also? If so, how? It has been observed that the solubility of gases generally decreases as temperature increases. More oxygen can dissolve in cold water, ensuring sufficient oxygen for aquatic life (Fig. 9.8). On the other hand, when water warms up, the solubility of oxygen decreases. Now I understand that the mixtures we use can be of two types—uniform and non-uniform. Uniform mixtures are called solutions, and their components are not visible separately. In non-uniform mixtures, the components can be seen either with the naked eye or with a magnifying device. I observed that in some non-uniform mixtures, such as sawdust in water, the sawdust floats, whereas in the mixture of sand and water, the sand sinks. I wonder why that happens?
